places.name: New Siberian Islands, Russia (Bunge Land and Kotelny)
places.wording: We found no published space-analog use here.
places.detail: Yes, polar science but no space-analog use found. Bunge Land is a 6,200 km2 bare sand plain between Kotelny and Faddeyevsky, studied by Russian and German permafrost teams (Schirrmeister and others 2010) and shown by NASA Earth Observatory. Kotelny had a research station and base from 1933 to 1993; the Temp airfield is now military.
places.not_checked: Whether the airfield or base operates now; permits (the area is a military zone). The article date was not shown.

evidence.claim: Bunge Land: about 6,200 km2 of sand, mostly under 8 m above the sea, origin studied by Schirrmeister et al. 2010

places.name: Nordaustlandet, Svalbard (Murchisonfjorden)
places.wording: This is not a little-known place. Published space-analog work exists for it.
places.detail: Yes, both. The ESA / Open University catalogue lists Murchison Fjord (79.88 N 18.49 E) as an AMASE Mars-analog site. The Kinnvika station in the same fjord was built for the International Geophysical Year 1957-58 and used again in 2007-09; it is empty now. The place is polar desert inside the Nordaust-Svalbard nature reserve. It is not a little-known place.
places.not_checked: Which AMASE years worked there; current landing and research permit rules of the reserve.

Kinnvika: built 1957-58 by a Swedish-Finnish-Swiss expedition, revived for the Polar Year 2007-09, inside the nature reserve

places.detail: Polar field work yes, space-analog none found. A Dutch team wintered at Kapp Lee in 1968-69, made summer visits to 1988, and came back with the SEES expeditions of 2015 and 2022. No staffed station today.

places.name: Iceland, south coast (Landeyjar sands)
places.wording: We found no published space-analog use here.
places.detail: No analog work found for this sand plain itself, but it sits inside the best-studied analog country: the catalogue's Eyjafjallajokull and Krysuvik sites are 55 to 70 km away, and NASA rover tests (SAND-E, 2019 and 2021) used sands near Langjokull. The challenge text itself calls Iceland widely studied.
places.not_checked: Icelandic-language sources; the small airfields at Hella and Bakki (coordinates not verified).

places.name: Vestfold Hills, Antarctica
places.wording: This is not a little-known place. Published space-analog work exists for it.
places.detail: Yes. Australia's year-round Davis station is at the edge of the hills, and the hypersaline Deep Lake there is studied as a model for cold Martian brines. It is a well-studied place, not a little-known one.
places.not_checked: The Mars-analog wording comes from a search summary of a 2026 paper we did not open. Davis's ski landing area and sea-ice runway (no airfield entry in the COMNAP file).

evidence.claim: Deep Lake: about 270 g/L salt, liquid to about -20 C, microbial community studied since the 1980s
Davis station in the COMNAP facilities list
